settings.name_in_paper: Decentralized multi-agent multi-armed bandits with Byzantine agents (fixed directed graph)
unmapped: N agents on a fixed directed communication graph; each agent observes its own reward stream
Byzantine agents may send arbitrary (and conflicting) arm counts and mean estimates to neighbors; each agent has at most f Byzantine neighbors and knows f
reward distributions of an arm may differ across agents but share the same mean
regret is per normal agent R_i(T) or summed over normal agents
settings.definition_quote: All agents face the same set of $M>1$ arms ... For each arm $k\in\scr M$, all its reward variables over the network $X_{i,k}(t)$, $i\in\scr V$ share the same mean $\mu_{k}$ while their distributions may be different. ... bounded support $[0,1]$ ... we assume that each agent has at most $f$ Byzantine neighbors, and knows the number $f$.

settings.name_in_paper: Decentralized multi-agent MAB with Byzantine agents over time-varying (random) graphs
unmapped: N agents on a time-varying directed communication graph G(t)
Byzantine agents may send arbitrary (and conflicting) information; each agent has at most f Byzantine neighbors and knows f
reward distributions of an arm may differ across agents but share the same mean
settings.definition_quote: This subsection extends theoretical results to the cases when neighbor graph $\bbb G(t)$ changes over time. Define $\scr N_i(t)$ as $\scr N_i^-(t)$ as the corresponding neighbor set and out-neighbor set of agent $i$ at time $t$.

algorithms.name: Resilient Decentralized UCB (with consistency and trimmed-mean filters)

symbols.N_i: number of neighbors of normal agent i
symbols.f: maximum number of Byzantine neighbors of any agent

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: The expected cumulative regret of any normal agent $i\in\scr H$ satisfies \liminf_{T\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R_i(T)}{\log T}\ge O\Big(\frac{\log T}{\max\{|\scr N_i|-2f+1,1\}}\Big).

results.notes: Statement is mathematically ill-formed (liminf of R/log T bounded below by O(log T/...)); the proof claims a lower bound of order Omega(log T / max{|N_i|-2f+1,1}) via informal argument for algorithms using trimmed filtering. Recorded as Omega on R_i(T).

symbols.G_i: max_{t in 1..T} g_{i,k}(t) log t for the suboptimal arm k being summed over, where g_{i,k}(t) <= 1 is the adjusted variance after filtering

conditions: each agent has at most f Byzantine neighbors

source.label: thm:complete
source.quote: The expected cumulative regret of any normal agent $i\in\scr H$ satisfies R_i(T) \le \min_{\tau\in\{1,\ldots,T\}}\Bigg(\sum_{k:\;\Delta_k>0}\bigg(\max_{t\in\{1,\ldots, \tau\}}\frac{8g_{i,k}(t)\log t}{\Delta_k}+\Big(1+\frac{\pi^2}{3}\Big)\Delta_k\bigg)+(T-\tau)\Delta_M\Bigg) \le \sum_{k:\;\Delta_k>0}\bigg(\max_{t\in\{1,\ldots, T\}}\frac{8g_{i,k}(t)\log t}{\Delta_k}+\Big(1+\frac{\pi^2}{3}\Big)\Delta_k\bigg).

results.notes: Recorded the second (looser) inequality; the first form takes a min over tau with an additional (T-tau)Delta_max term. Regret defined via means, hence pseudo-regret. Algorithm uses log t, so treated as anytime though T is listed as input. Theorem 7 gives the same bound for time-varying graphs.

conditions: each agent has at most f Byzantine neighbors

source.label: thm:noworse
source.quote: The regret for each normal agent $i\in\scr H$ is always no worse than that of the single-agent UCB1, i.e., R_i(T)\le\sum_{k:\;\Delta_k>0}\bigg(\frac{8\log T}{\Delta_k}+\Big(1+\frac{\pi^2}{3}\Big)\Delta_k\bigg).

conditions: each agent has at least 3f+1 neighbors
each agent has at most f Byzantine neighbors

source.label: thm:outperform
source.quote: If each agent has at least $3f+1$ neighbors, then the cumulative regret of all normal agents is strictly better than that of the non-cooperative counterpart: R(T)=\sum_{i\in\scr H} R_i(T)<|\scr H|\sum_{k:\;\Delta_k>0}\bigg(\frac{8\log T}{\Delta_k}+\Big(1+\frac{\pi^2}{3}\Big)\Delta_k\bigg).

results.notes: Strict inequality on network total regret (sum over normal agents).

symbols.p: probability that every agent has at least 3f+1 neighbors at each time

conditions: at each time, every agent has at least 3f+1 neighbors with probability p in (0,1]
each agent has at most f Byzantine neighbors

source.label: thm:random
source.quote: If the probability that every agent in the network has at least $3f+1$ neighbors is $p\in(0,1]$ at each time $t$, then the network total regret is strictly better than the non-cooperative counterpart, i.e., \eqref{eq:better} holds.

results.notes: Remark 3: for p in (0,1) the improvement is only O(1).

symbols.N_max_i: max over t of the number of neighbors of agent i at time t
symbols.f: maximum number of Byzantine neighbors of any agent

source.label: thm:tvlower
source.quote: For any time-varying neighbor graph sequence $\{\bbb G(t)\}$, the expected cumulative regret of any normal agent $i\in\scr H$ satisfies \liminf_{T\rightarrow\infty}\frac{R_i(T)}{\log T}\ge O\Big(\frac{\log T}{\max\{\max_{t}|\scr N_i(t)|-2f+1,1\}}\Big).

results.notes: Ill-formed statement as in Theorem 1; interpreted as Omega lower bound on R_i(T).
